sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Flow cytometry confirmed surface display of the myc-tagged N-terminus in control T cells; western blot confirmed total protein expression. No CD5 signalling or ligand-binding assay was reported in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: CD5 has exactly one extracellular terminus: the mature N-terminus beginning at residue 25 (after the 1–24 signal peptide). The paper places a myc epitope 'on the N-terminus' of the full-length construct, so the junction is unambiguously after the signal-peptide cleavage site. Computed position: insert_after_residue = 24 (G), residue_after = 25 (R), 357 residues from the TM boundary — well clear of any constraint. The C-terminal FLAG and mScarlet tags from the same paper land in the intracellular tail (residues 399–495) and are recorded in other_positions. Full-length, membrane-anchored CD5 bearing a myc epitope on the N-terminus and a FLAG tag on the C-terminus was ectopically expressed in primary human T cells (endogenous CD5 knocked out by CRISPR-Cas9). Surface display of the tagged construct was confirmed by flow cytometry and total protein by western blot.

sources.claim: To investigate whether the lack of CD5 detection was due to the loss of CD5 protein, we removed the endogenous CD5 gene using CRISRP-Cas9 and ectopically expressed an engineered CD5 construct tagged with a myc epitope on the N terminus and with a FLAG tag on the C terminus ( Figure 1 G).

literature_notes: Five ledger lines (L1–L5) all derive from a single PMC paper (PMC11293353). L1/L2/L5 describe the same dual-tagged (myc N-terminal / FLAG C-terminal) CD5 construct; L3/L4 describe a C-terminal mScarlet fusion. The myc tag on the extracellular N-terminus is the only surface-facing tag in the ledger and yields one site. The FLAG (L1/L5) and mScarlet (L3/L4) C-terminal fusions both land in the intracellular tail (topology: IC 399–495) and are therefore not surface tag sites; they are recorded in other_positions. No ledger line reports any insertion in an internal extracellular loop of CD5, so no internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: FLAG tag placed on the C-terminus of full-length CD5; the C-terminus (residue 495) lies in the intracellular tail (IC: 399–495), so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the cell surface.
mScarlet fluorescent protein fused to the C-terminus of full-length CD5 for live-imaging; same intracellular position (IC: 399–495), not a surface tag.
